extracted.intended_audience: media researchers, journalists, policymakers, and students interested in India's media environment
extracted.subtask_description: A country profile summarising key metrics and developments shaping India’s news ecosystem (trust, platform use, legal/regulatory changes, press freedom indicators) based on the Reuters Institute / Digital News Report data and reporting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Trust in news overall
rubrics_metrics.description: 41% — Overall trust in news increased slightly in this election year (41%).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Among survey respondents, large legacy media brands tend to retain the highest levels of trust (including public broadcasters like the BBC and All India Radio). Partisan commercial broadcasters and independent digital portals who are either uncritical or extremely critical of those in positions of power are actively distrusted by the respondents. Note: 'scores should not be seen as a measure of the quality or trustworthiness of the content itself.'

rubrics_metrics.name: RSF World Press Freedom Index
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measure of press freedom from NGO Reporters Without Borders based on expert assessment (link to rsf.org provided). Use as an external index of the national press freedom environment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Share news via social, messaging or email
rubrics_metrics.description: 45% — Proportion of respondents who share news via social, messaging or email.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This metric captures propensity to share news items through informal networks; relevant when assessing news reach and informal circulation channels.

rubrics_metrics.name: Internet penetration
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contextual demographic metric indicating the share of population with internet access — constrains digital news reach and shapes platform strategies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Platform usage for news
rubrics_metrics.description: Almost half of respondents use YouTube (54%) and WhatsApp (48%) for news each week; Facebook and X are becoming less popular.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Legacy platforms such as NDTV, Times of India, Republic TV, and BBC News continue to enjoy high viewership in offline and online products among younger, urban, mostly English-speaking sample. Print (40%) and TV (46%) remain popular platforms — important to weigh platform reach by demographic.

rubrics_metrics.name: Methodology and sample limitations
rubrics_metrics.description: These data are based on a survey of mainly English-speaking, online news users in India – a small subset of a larger, more diverse, media market.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Findings in this online poll are not nationally representative and will tend to under-represent the continued importance of traditional media such as TV and print. Interpret poll-derived metrics (trust, platform use) with this sampling bias in mind.

rubrics_metrics.name: Legal and regulatory changes affecting press freedom
rubrics_metrics.description: New laws (Digital Personal Data Protection Act, Press and Registration of Periodicals Act, Telecommunications Act 2023) have given or could give sweeping regulatory powers to government bodies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specific concerns: DPDP gives powers to government-appointed board members and lacks journalist exemptions to access personal data; the Press and Registration Act creates unspecified powers for government to issue guidelines or make rules; the Telecommunications Act 2023 has broad definitions of telecommunication services and raises concerns about surveillance, internet shutdowns, and government access to encrypted social media messages. These legal changes should be treated as structural risks to press freedom and to how news can be reported and distributed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Judicial intervention and transparency measures
rubrics_metrics.description: Supreme Court put government plan to make a ministry fact-check unit the core place to flag false information on hold and struck down electoral bonds (directing SBI to release information).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Court rulings can check executive actions that affect freedom of speech (fact-checking body) and can increase transparency (electoral bonds decision). Such rulings also create opportunities for investigative journalism (e.g., collaborations to examine electoral funding).

rubrics_metrics.name: Coverage quality: context and balance
rubrics_metrics.description: National and regional media’s coverage of the tensions between Kuki and Meitei communities (Manipur) was found lacking context and balance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess coverage for contextual reporting and balance, especially on communal/ethnic violence; failure to provide context can exacerbate tensions and erode trust. Independent fact-finding (e.g., Editors’ Guild report) is a relevant benchmark.

rubrics_metrics.name: Misinformation dynamics
rubrics_metrics.description: Widespread misinformation via WhatsApp and other social media fuelled tensions in Manipur and elsewhere.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Misinformation spread via private and semi-private platforms is a major risk to public safety and to the informational role of news organisations; mitigation and verification strategies are essential when producing news content.

rubrics_metrics.name: Internet shutdowns and restrictions
rubrics_metrics.description: Internet ban imposed by the government during Manipur tensions adversely affected free flow of information for reporters within the region and alienated the rest of the country from crucial developments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Connectivity restrictions are operational constraints on newsgathering and distribution; they also have implications for timeliness and comprehensiveness of reporting and for citizens’ right to information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Media ownership and corporatisation
rubrics_metrics.description: Adani Group’s expansion into media (control of NDTV, increased stake in IANS, acquisition in BQ Prime) reflects increasing corporatisation of media in India.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ownership concentration and corporate influence are structural factors that may affect editorial independence, plurality, and the landscape of credible sources; consider ownership when evaluating news ecosystems or homepage sourcing decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Repressive actions against media organisations
rubrics_metrics.description: Raids on NewsClick offices and residences, device seizures, investigations by agencies, and use of terrorism charges have been criticised by journalists’ unions as 'chilling' and an effort to muzzle press freedom.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State enforcement actions (raids, legal charges, seizures) are indicators of a hostile environment for journalism; they affect safety, willingness to publish investigative content, and the availability of independent outlets.

rubrics_metrics.name: Opportunities for collaborative investigative reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: The Supreme Court ruling on electoral bonds provided opportunities for digital platforms such as NewsLaundry and The News Minute to collaborate on investigative stories about electoral funding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Legal openings and released data can enable collaborative investigations across digital outlets, increasing accountability reporting; news-homepage curation should prioritise such original investigations when assessing newsworthiness and public interest.
